extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed final mechanism ontology cleanup from automated locator notes. The paper supports antimicrobial phenotype, nisin P structure/modification context, and microbiota treatment effects; no direct molecular target mechanism is overclaimed.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Purified nisin P showed source-supported antibacterial activity and MIC values against selected natural nisin producers, lactobacilli, staphylococci, and other tested indicator strains, generally less potent than nisin A.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: purified nisin P compared with nisin A

supports: Tables 3 and 4 report well-diffusion activity classes and MIC values for nisin P and nisin A.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=25:Cross- immunity assays; xml:sec=26:Spectrum of inhibitory activity; xml:sec=27:Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) assays
supports: Methods define purified peptide well-diffusion and MIC assays.

mechanism_claims.limitations: This supports antibacterial phenotype and potency comparison, not a direct molecular target or pore-formation assay in this paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: LC-MS/MS and tryptic peptide evidence support the nisin P peptide sequence/modification context, and the discussion links reduced activity to shorter C-terminus plus incomplete rings B/E as a structure-activity hypothesis.

supports: Table 2 lists nisin P tryptic peptides, m/z, PSM, CAM, and probability values.
Figures 5-7 support purified peptide mass, MS/MS fragmentation/ring context, and final modified structure depiction.
Discussion frames structural differences and incomplete ring formation as likely contributors to reduced activity.

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper discusses known nisin/lipid-II and hinge-region context but does not directly assay lipid-II binding, membrane insertion, pore formation, or target binding for nisin P.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Faecal fermentation/qPCR experiments showed treatment-dependent effects on live bacterial counts, with nisin P and H treatments closer to total-cell counts than nisin A in the prose summary.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: nisin A/P/H faecal fermentation treatment context

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=11:Nisin activity in faecal fermentation; xml:fig=9
supports: Results and Figure 9 describe total bacteria/live-cell qPCR outcomes after 15 μM and 50 μM nisin treatments at 8 and 24 h.
Methods define faecal fermentation dosing, second-dose design, DNA extraction/EMA treatment, and 16S qPCR readout.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure-level exact nisin P/H values were not converted from plotted panels; this claim is retained only as contextual microbiota activity evidence, not MIC/toxicity or direct mechanism.
